target_customer: Celebrities and their fans, with charities as beneficiaries
problem: Celebrities have fan reach but no simple way to direct fan donations to causes they care about.
business_model: Likely a fee on donations; no source states it

founders.name: Josef Teplow
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by VentureBeat at Demo Day, March 2012; YC page lists no founders

competitors.name: Crowdrise
competitors.what: Online fundraising platform built around celebrity campaigns

competitors.name: Prizeo
competitors.what: YC backed celebrity prize and charity campaigns

technical_complexity.rationale: Payments and a social campaign page are standard web engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Value depended on signing celebrities, which is hard for one person, while the software itself was copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copy found; the company went inactive.

market_need_then: A Givespark test campaign with a few celebrities raised 87,000 USD for bone marrow transplants, per VentureBeat in March 2012.

branding.brand_signature: Pitch line: Twitter, just with money

brand_strength.rationale: The only brand evidence is a Demo Day tagline quoted by VentureBeat.

outcome_analysis: Givespark presented a celebrity charity fundraising idea at YC Demo Day in March 2012 with a one person team and a small test campaign. No funding, traction beyond that test, or shutdown account was found, so the cause of its inactive status is not public and no failure factors are assigned.
notes: Website givespark.com returned HTTP 503. Outcome search found no cause. Prizeo source is 8 months after the batch. A Crunchbase page found for GiveSpark is an unrelated advisory firm and was ignored. Founders' education and employers not found.
